LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_BlackHoleSu: Replace the home system's star with a black hole
Permanently replaces the home system's star with a black hole, present from the start of the game. You can switch it on or off at any time, including mid-game, and the change applies immediately.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_BlackHoleLi: Fraction of normal sunlight the black hole lets through. Affects both map brightness and the sky's colour tint. 100% looks like an ordinary star; lower values are dimmer, with a colder, near-black cast. Has no effect while the black hole is switched off.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_BlackHoleGr: The black hole's apparent size on the world map slowly increases the longer it has existed. Switch off to keep it a fixed size forever.

How fast the black hole grows. 1.0 means the disc's on-screen area doubles every in-game year (its radius grows by about 41% per year). Higher values grow faster; 0 stops growth without switching it off.

Ceiling on how large the black hole can grow, as a multiple of its starting radius. At the default of 8x its disc spans the full height of the screen. Prevents an old colony from ending up with an all-black world map.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_RefurbishCo: Multiplies the plasteel and advanced component cost of the Refurbish gizmo on the cerebrex core, per point of hit points restored. Higher values make repairing the core more expensive; lower values make it cheaper.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_CoreRetreat: The fraction of the cerebrex core's max hit points that must be destroyed before a core-focused raid gives up and retreats. Lower values make raiders retreat sooner; higher values let them press the attack longer, up to the point of destroying the core outright.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_StrategySel: Multiplies how often the storyteller picks a raid strategy that targets the cerebrex core (core strike, sappers, or siege) instead of an ordinary raid. Set to 0 to disable these raid types entirely.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_LatticeEnab: Master switch for feeding the cerebrex core steel to spread mechanoid lattice terrain, and for the biome conversion and mood effects that follow from it. Requires Alpha Biomes; has no effect if that mod isn't loaded.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_LatticeStee: How much steel is consumed to convert one map cell to lattice terrain. Higher values make the spread more expensive to sustain at the same pace.
The lattice stops drawing steel once your stockpile would fall below this amount, and only resumes once it recovers comfortably above it. Protects a baseline reserve for construction and repairs.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_LatticeTarg: How many in-game days a constant, uninterrupted steel stream takes to convert the entire map. Lower values make the spread faster; higher values make it slower.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_LatticeDlaF: Roughly how much of the spread is spent on branching tendrils versus filling in behind them. Higher values keep the spread stringier for longer; lower values thicken it faster.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_LatticeRunn: Chance that a tendril's growth point becomes a long-range runner, seeding an isolated island of lattice terrain ahead of the main spread. 0 disables runners entirely.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_BiomeFlipTh: The fraction of convertible map cells that must be covered in lattice terrain before this world tile's biome permanently changes to mechanoid intrusion. This cannot be undone once it happens.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Settings_MoodBuffSca: Multiplies the mood bonus colonists get from living in or near the mechanoid lattice. Set to 0 to disable the mood effect entirely.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_Lattice_Gizmo_Desc: Draws steel from your stockpiles to slowly spread mechanoid lattice terrain outward from the core. This will destroy plants and permanently sterilize the ground it covers - it cannot be reversed. If enough of the map is converted, the region's biome will change forever.
LanguageData.CerebrexFlavourPack_BiomeFlipped_LetterT:
The mechanoid lattice has consumed enough of {0} that the region itself has become a mechanoid intrusion biome.
This is permanent. The following are now gone: - Hunting: wild animal density collapses to near-zero. Only rats and guinea pigs remain. - Fishing: this region can no longer support fish. Existing fishing spots are dead. - Caravan foraging: forageability drops to zero. Caravans leaving from here carry no foraged food. - Wild flora: native plant species will not regrow. Only hardy grass and sessile mechanoid growths spread. - Rainfall: rain becomes rare. Expect clear skies, fog, and dry thunderstorms.
Caravans will also move more slowly across this tile.
